transcript.text: Many ovens won't heat at all after a power cut (or with an end time set) until the clock is set or manual mode is selected — often a hand symbol, or holding two buttons together; the manual shows how. Was the clock flashing or set to an auto / timer mode, or was it already showing the time in manual mode?
Yes the clock is flashing 0.00 and a little symbol. Power went off for an hour last night. How do I set it? I haven't got the manual

Thanks for letting me know about the flashing clock. I have noted the 0.00 code shown on the display; this step is the right place to start regardless of that reading as it helps identify which part has failed. Please take care, as the oven and grill get hot quickly, so use oven gloves and do not touch the elements. If you try the grill on its own for a few minutes, does it heat — and does the main oven heat at all?
nothing heats, the knobs do nothing at all. I just need to know how to set the clock, can you tell me?

Thanks for letting us know about the cold grill and main oven. With the clock flashing, please take care as the oven and grill get hot quickly; use oven gloves and do not touch the elements. With the oven set to fan mode, look through the door at the fan cover at the back. Can you see or hear the fan turning?
Nothing happens with the knobs, no fan or light. Can you just tell me how to set the clock? I haven't got the manual

[Heading: Oven fan motor]
Thank you for letting us know about the fan issue. Based on your reports that the fan is not turning and the grill is cold, along with the displayed code 0.00, the oven fan motor appears to be the likely cause. Please note that this code is a controller report only and does not prove a part has failed. I am not recommending you replace any parts yourself; an appliance engineer can confirm the issue safely.
